content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?From Quarks to Quasars's PostFrom Quarks to QuasarsMarch 23 at 10:00 AM · Shared with PublicEarth’s magnetic field is being disturbed by solar activity.A G3 level geomagnetic storm was detected on March 22, caused by a stream of fast moving solar particles interacting with Earth’s magnetic field. These storms can last hours to over a day and vary in intensity.The main visible effect could be auroras appearing farther from the poles than usual, especially in dark, clear skies.There may also be minor impacts on technology. Power grids can experience small fluctuations, satellites may be affected, and GPS signals can become less accurate.For most people, the biggest effect will be in the sky.If conditions are right tonight, you might be able to see the northern lights much farther south than usual.Learn more:NOAA Space Weather Prediction CenterAll reactions:1226 comments52 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Jefferey BurnsideThis is why our Earth has protection from this that no other planet planet yet discovered has.1wView 1 replyPhilip SymesPlanetary alignment just happened 1wSherlene HutsellGIPHY1wDaniel PalmerSolar Max.
